decision.rationale: Partir du meilleur programme mesuré et correct, T2 (7,331 μs), et y adapter la réduction warp-first de T1, source correcte à 29,552 μs. T2 réduit des tuiles de 4096 éléments avec 128 threads et des sommes intermédiaires 64 bits; remplacer le seul combine CTA partagé par une réduction warp-first est une hypothèse de composition concrète. Préserver les accumulateurs 64 bits et toutes les contraintes du contrat; mesurer et vérifier le programme intégré sans supposer un gain additif. T3 est écarté de cette combinaison : ses mesures correctes sont environ 762 μs.

children.objective: Using AB-MCTS, isolate the block-local reduction mechanism: replace the modulo/shared-memory tree with a warp-first reduction and cross-warp combine while retaining the 128-element tile and recursive host-stage structure where feasible. Do not assume signed int32 partial sums are safe merely because the final sum fits; use exact intermediate arithmetic (e.g. wider partials) or a rigorously correct modular representation and final conversion. Preserve tail handling, ABI, default stream, scratch bounds, and every valid n (including n=0 if valid under the official domain). Report failed attempts, correctness results, and repeated full-program timings; this is a hypothesis about local reduction cost, not a proven bottleneck.
children.subject: Warp-first block reduction

children.objective: Using AB-MCTS, focus on the conventional multi-kernel hierarchy: vary tile/grain size and partial-count/finalization strategy to test lower-launch-count designs, including but not assuming a two-pass design wins. Avoid repeating a broad warp-reduction sweep already assigned to T1; use a straightforward correct CTA reduction unless tuning it is necessary to realize a hierarchy. Preserve exact arithmetic for all valid inputs, including safe intermediate sums, uninitialized scratch, tails, ABI, and default-stream behavior. If n=0 is valid, produce the empty sum. Report failures, correctness, and repeated full-program timings, then compare against the supplied baseline without treating one launch-count hypothesis as the result.
children.subject: Fewer launches with a two-pass hierarchy

children.objective: Using AB-MCTS, investigate the distinct cooperative single-kernel path: resident CTAs compute grid-stride partials, synchronize grid-wide, and one CTA writes the result. The CUDA 12.6.3 guide documents the needed cooperative launch/grid synchronization, but that does not establish effective runtime support or performance on this measured target; validate the actual launch and include host-side setup/query costs in full-program timings. Ensure residency-safe configuration, exact intermediate arithmetic, no reliance on initialized scratch or atomics, and correctness for every valid n (including n=0 if valid). Record unsupported, incorrect, or slower attempts; only return a correctly validated candidate.
children.subject: Single-launch cooperative reduction
